# Champions of the Future

## Lead

Champions of the Future (often abbreviated as COTF) is an international karting series launched in 2020 and organized by RGMMC Group, a Switzerland-based motorsport promoter. The series stages multi-round championships primarily for OK and OK-Junior classes under the CIK-FIA technical framework, and positions itself as a high-level preparatory competition that closely mirrors circuits, sporting procedures, and technical conditions used in FIA Karting European and World Championship events. Its events are live-streamed globally and frequently covered by specialist karting media, which highlight its role in talent development within the single-seater pathway. The scope of this article is the karting series organized by RGMMC under the “Champions of the Future” banner; other unrelated uses of the phrase are not covered here. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com), [RGMMC Group – Official Site](https://www.rgmmc.com), [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news)

## Identity and Notability

Champions of the Future is an international karting championship platform:
- Domain and scope: multi-event, professional-level karting competition in Europe, targeted at OK and OK-Junior categories that feed into FIA single-seater talent pipelines. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com)
- Founding and organizer: launched by RGMMC Group in 2020; RGMMC is a Swiss promoter known for organizing high-profile karting series and promotion activities for international karting. [RGMMC Group – Official Site](https://www.rgmmc.com)
- Relationship to governing frameworks: events run to the CIK-FIA technical basis (chassis, engine homologation, tyres and fuel practices aligned with OK/OK-Junior categories), with sporting procedures and scrutineering modeled on international standards and implemented under local ASN permits. [FIA Karting – Technical/Homologation Overview](https://www.fiakarting.com/homologations), [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news)
- Purpose and positioning: the series is described by its organizer and covered by independent karting media as a “preparatory” or “warm-up” competition for major FIA Karting championships, often scheduled on the same circuits ahead of European or World events, attracting factory and top private teams. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com), [Vroom Kart – COTF Event Coverage](https://www.vroomkart.com/news)
- Notability: COTF events are consistently reported in specialist outlets (e.g., Vroom Kart) and referenced by FIA Karting communications when noting preparatory racing or venue familiarity among competitors, indicating the series’ relevance in the elite OK/OK-Junior sphere. [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news), [Vroom Kart – COTF Event Coverage](https://www.vroomkart.com/news)

## History and Development

- Launch and early phase (2020): COTF debuted in 2020, a season shaped by the COVID-19 pandemic and public-health restrictions across Europe. Despite disruptions, the series delivered rounds used by top teams to prepare for FIA Karting pinnacle events, including Portimão, which hosted the FIA Karting World Championships that year. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com), [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news)
- Consolidation (2021–2022): The series consolidated an annual “Euro Series” format with multi-round calendars on established European circuits such as Zuera (Spain), Genk (Belgium), Kristianstad (Sweden), Lonato and Franciacorta (Italy), and Portimão (Portugal). Factory teams across major chassis brands (e.g., Tony Kart, KR/IAME, Parolin, Birel ART) routinely entered, reinforcing the championship’s competitive depth. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com), [Vroom Kart – COTF Event Coverage](https://www.vroomkart.com/news)
- Expansion and refinement (2023–2025): COTF maintained the Euro Series and added or trialed early-season “Winter” formats and calendar refinements to continue mirroring FIA schedules. The series’ organization emphasized Super Heats and detailed sporting procedures similar to FIA Karting events, helping teams benchmark performance and logistics. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com), [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news)

## Organization and Governance

- Promoter: RGMMC Group (RGMMC Group SA), headquartered in Switzerland, acts as the organizer and promoter. The group’s leadership is responsible for calendar construction, sporting format, event production, stewarding appointments, and media operations in line with ASN authorizations. [RGMMC Group – Official Site](https://www.rgmmc.com)
- Key personnel and officials: The series employs experienced race directors, technical delegates, and stewards familiar with FIA Karting and CIK-FIA procedures, executing scrutineering and sporting oversight at each event. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com)
- Regulatory framework: Technical rules follow the CIK-FIA OK and OK-Junior homologations (chassis, engines, tyres, fuel), with event-specific supplementary regulations, bulletins, and official notices published by the series. [FIA Karting – Homologations](https://www.fiakarting.com/homologations), [Champions of the Future – Documents/Regulations](https://www.championskarting.com)

## Competition Format and Classes

- Classes: OK (senior) and OK-Junior form the core of COTF competition; eligibility follows international karting age criteria set by CIK-FIA guidance via national ASNs. [FIA Karting – Sporting framework](https://www.fiakarting.com/regulations), [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com)
- Event structure: Typical weekends include free practice, qualifying practice, multiple qualifying heats (grids set by time), Super Heats, and Finals per class. Grid sizes are capped per circuit homologation, with split groups when entries exceed capacity. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com)
- Points and standings: Points are awarded across Heats/Super Heats and Finals to determine round results and cumulative championship standings. The series publishes detailed points tables and final classifications at the end of each season. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com)
- Equipment and suppliers: COTF aligns with OK/OK-Junior homologations. Tyres and fuel used at events are selected within homologated supplier frameworks commonly used in FIA Karting (e.g., LeCont tyres and Panta Racing Fuel have been specified for OK/OK-Junior in FIA Karting), enabling consistency in performance and setup. [FIA Karting – Homologations](https://www.fiakarting.com/homologations), [LeCont Tyres – Official](https://lecont.it/), [Panta Racing Fuel – Official](https://pantaracingfuel.it/)
- Scrutineering and controls: Scrutineering covers chassis and engine identification, tyre scanning/control, fuel conformity, and parc fermé procedures, with on-event bulletins overseeing compliance and steward decisions. [Champions of the Future – Documents/Regulations](https://www.championskarting.com)

## Circuits and Geographic Spread

- Representative circuits: COTF has scheduled rounds on major European venues, including:
 - Kartódromo Internacional do Algarve (Portimão, Portugal)
 - Circuito Internacional de Zuera (Spain)
 - Karting Genk: Home of Champions (Belgium)
 - Åsum Ring – Kristianstad Karting (Sweden)
 - South Garda Karting – Lonato (Italy)
 - Franciacorta Karting Track (Italy)
 - Kartodromo Internacional de Portimão and other FIA Karting host circuits as applicable to annual calendars
 Coverage and official calendars reflect a largely European footprint consistent with OK/OK-Junior competition hubs. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com), [Vroom Kart – COTF Event Coverage](https://www.vroomkart.com/news)

## Seasons and Results (2020–2025)

- 2020: Inaugural season delivered despite COVID-19 disruptions, with events used as preparation for FIA Karting European and World Championships; season standings and final classifications were published by the series. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com)
- 2021–2022: Multi-round Euro Series formats standardized, with standings per class (OK, OK-Junior) and winners recognized across rounds and overall championships; independent reports highlighted close competition among factory-supported drivers. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com), [Vroom Kart – COTF Event Coverage](https://www.vroomkart.com/news)
- 2023–2025: The series continued its annual cadence; calendars comprised 3–5 European rounds per season, featuring Super Heats and Finals on FIA Karting venues. Full classification lists and champions per class were published on the official site and covered by specialist media. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com), [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news), [Vroom Kart – COTF Event Coverage](https://www.vroomkart.com/news)

Note: Detailed, year-by-year champions and event-by-event winners are maintained in official COTF standings and event result archives, with independent outlets publishing round reports and analyses for each season. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com), [Vroom Kart – COTF Event Coverage](https://www.vroomkart.com/news)

## Notable Competitors and Alumni

COTF has featured many drivers who progressed into FIA Formula 4, Formula Regional, FIA Formula 3 and FIA Formula 2:
- Andrea Kimi Antonelli: Competed in international OK/OK-Junior karting before moving into F4 and beyond, widely covered as a Mercedes-AMG junior driver. His karting trajectory appears in independent coverage of elite OK-level series, including preparatory events. [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news)
- Arvid Lindblad: Red Bull Junior Team driver who raced at the top level in OK/OK-Junior competition, then advanced into FIA F4 and FIA F3. [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news)
- Freddie Slater: A leading OK-Junior and OK competitor who progressed into single-seaters (F4/FRECA) with coverage noting his karting success prior to car racing. [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news)
- Tuukka Taponen: Ferrari Driver Academy driver with top-level OK achievements before moving into FIA F4/F3 pathways, referenced by independent karting coverage and FIA Karting. [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news)

Independent karting outlets and FIA Karting reports commonly cite Champions of the Future rounds as relevant preparatory stages for these drivers, particularly on circuits later used for European or World title events. [Vroom Kart – COTF Event Coverage](https://www.vroomkart.com/news), [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news)

## Media, Coverage, and Audience

- Live streaming: COTF produces live streams across full race weekends via its official video channels, including YouTube, with multi-camera coverage, timing graphics, and commentary. [Champions of the Future – YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@ChampionsKarting)
- Specialist media coverage: Event previews, results, and analyses are routinely published by independent karting media such as Vroom Kart; FIA Karting communications also reference preparatory races and driver form. [Vroom Kart – COTF Event Coverage](https://www.vroomkart.com/news), [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news)
- Social media: The series maintains official channels (e.g., Instagram) for announcements, highlights, and schedules. [Champions of the Future – Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/championskarting)

## Sponsorships and Partners

- Technical alignment: The series’ use of equipment and consumables is aligned with homologated OK/OK-Junior frameworks (e.g., tyre and fuel suppliers used in FIA Karting). This enables realistic benchmarking for teams preparing for FIA events. [FIA Karting – Homologations](https://www.fiakarting.com/homologations), [LeCont Tyres – Official](https://lecont.it/), [Panta Racing Fuel – Official](https://pantaracingfuel.it/)
- Event production partners: Timing, live streaming production, and on-event logistics are organized by RGMMC with specialist vendors; details are published within event-specific supplementary regulations and organizer communications. [Champions of the Future – Documents/Regulations](https://www.championskarting.com)

## Safety, Stewarding, and Regulations

- Stewarding and appeals: The series applies international karting sporting codes, with appointed stewards issuing decisions and time penalties; procedural details are codified in supplementary regulations and event bulletins. [Champions of the Future – Documents/Regulations](https://www.championskarting.com), [FIA Karting – Regulations](https://www.fiakarting.com/regulations)
- Safety standards: Parc fermé, scrutineering, flagging and race control procedures mirror international norms; circuit homologations and safety layouts are those used for OK/OK-Junior competition in Europe. [FIA Karting – Regulations](https://www.fiakarting.com/regulations)

## Reception, Impact, and Criticism

- Role in talent development: Independent media and FIA Karting communications often acknowledge COTF as providing high-quality race mileage on FIA-caliber circuits before major championships, with attendance by factory squads that elevates competitive level. [FIA Karting – News](https://www.fiakarting.com/news), [Vroom Kart – COTF Event Coverage](https://www.vroomkart.com/news)
- Criticisms and debates: Specialist outlets occasionally discuss topics familiar across OK/OK-Junior racing, such as race-incident penalties, track limits enforcement, and tyre/fuel management strategies; these are part of broader karting discourse rather than series-specific controversies. [Vroom Kart – Opinion/Features](https://www.vroomkart.com/news)

## Naming and Disambiguation

Champions of the Future, as covered here, refers to the international karting series promoted by RGMMC Group. Other unrelated uses of the phrase exist in general parlance across sports and education but are not substantiated by reliable motorsport sources for inclusion here. This article’s scope is confined to the karting series. [Champions of the Future – Official Site](https://www.championskarting.com), [RGMMC Group – Official Site](https://www.rgmmc.com)

champions of the future

Launched in 2020 by promoter RGMMC, the Champions of the Future series has become a must for the best international drivers and teams. Some of the biggest names in the world have already won the competition, some of them now in single-seaters. In 2024, the Champions of the Future Euro Series will be held over five meetings optimally spread between March and September. Based on the FIA Karting regulations, this season promises to be rich in quality and quantity in the OK and OK-Junior categories.

Minerva’s Virtual Academy offers bespoke education for racers aged 12 – 18. Unlike traditional schools, the Academy can be accessed anywhere in the world, at any time, and offers a world-class, flexible education fit for the 21st century. Pupils no longer have to miss school to attend training, track events, or race weekends.

The online school, which has won many awards since its launch, is run by Lawrence Tubb, a former head of department at Wycombe Abbey (one of the UK’s most prestigious private schools), and blends smart, interactive self-study (supported by the pupil’s personal mentor) with live online classes that can be managed around the athletes’ schedule. Young racers in particular are assisted by a unique mentoring programme that helps to develop them professionally as well as academically, overseeing their mental wellbeing whilst teaching soft skills such as public-speaking, self-confidence, and self-discipline.

Its pupils, who are able to choose from over 20 subjects at GCSE or A Level, are welcomed into a thriving, global community of talented pupils in sport and the arts, including Olympic hopefuls, West End performers, musicians, actors, and social media influencers, setting them up with brilliant friendships and connections for later on in life.

For the most bespoke solution (very popular in karting), private tutors from the school provide 1-2-1 teaching either in person or online, to ensure the pupil receives maximum attention and support on their path to success.

**MOL Group Italy non teme le sfide e le alimenta con la sua energia: Panta Racing fuels your ambitions!**

La Divisione Racing di Panta Distribuzione nasce nel 1989 e si distingue fin da subito per la ricerca tecnologica e lo sviluppo costante di nuovi prodotti per le competizioni.

**Panta Racing sviluppa e produce:**

*   prodotti per auto e moto da competizione, per garantire le migliori performance in gara;
*   un’ ampia gamma di prodotti speciali, per le più importanti case automobilistiche.

Panta Racing, grazie alla ricerca continua di eccellenza e alla qualità garantita in totale conformità con le normative FIM e FIA, è diventata **fornitore ufficiale dei più importanti Campionati Italiani, Europei ed Internazionali**, tra i quali spiccano**la serie internazionale GT Open e il Campionato mondiale kart CIK FIA.**

Grazie alla sua organizzazione logistica ed ad una rete di rivenditori professionali e preparati, PANTA distribuisce i propri prodotti racing in tutto il mondo ed è a fianco del successo sportivo di molti team.

![Image 1: Three Honda Civics race around a track, the front car emblazoned with the number 5](https://molgroupitaly.it/images/molitaly/content/prodotti_e_servizi/prodotti_petroliferi/prodotti_per_auto_e_moto_da_competizione/prodotti_per_auto_da_competizione-cover.jpg)

Benzina specifica per motori preparati, benzine con altissimo numero di ottano, benzine per auto d'epoca, diesel da competizione fino alla **benzina ufficiale del Campionato internazionale GT Open**.

![Image 2: Motorcyclist in red and black racing suit leans into a turn on a racetrack](https://molgroupitaly.it/images/molitaly/content/prodotti_e_servizi/prodotti_petroliferi/prodotti_per_auto_e_moto_da_competizione/prodotti_per_moto_da_competizione-cover.jpg)

Le benzine per moto di Panta Racing sono presenti nei Campionati più importanti come il **Word Super Bike (WSBK)** e **British Superbike (BSB)**.
